chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

When I was taken up for the Ascension, I saw a womb hanging from the Throne complaining to its Lord about another womb. I asked it, 'How many fathers are between you and it?' It said, 'We meet in the fortieth father.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet see hanging from the Throne during his Ascension?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal illustrates the metaphysical reality of kinship (silat al-rahim) by depicting a womb hanging from the Throne, emphasizing that maintaining family ties is a divine obligation with the power to expiate major sins. The specific mention of 'forty fathers' underscores the depth of ancestral connection, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence regarding inheritance and marital prohibitions.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-13 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Vasha, on the authority of Abil Hassan Al-Ridha (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “

When I was taken up for the Ascension, I saw that a womb was hanging from God’s Throne and was complaining to God about another womb. I asked it, ‘How much is the distance between you and him?’ The womb replied, ‘We are related to each other in the fortieth father in our lineage.’”
